evidence.excerpt: However, Figure 6 directly contradicts this claim. While the galaxies are indeed below the main sequence (solid black line), at least three members (including DD-78, DD-76, and ZF-COS-18842) are plotted *above* the dashed grey line, which is explicitly labeled as "-1 dex below".

judge_panel.reason: The paper states 'All members are located more than 1 dex below the star-forming main-sequence (P. Popesso et al. 2023)' and Figure 6 shows SFR on a log scale. Looking at Figure 6, the galaxies appear to be near or straddling the -1 dex dashed line, but the SFR values in Table 2 (e.g., DD-78 at 6.9 M☉/yr, ZF-COS-18842 at 4.9 M☉/yr) are indeed well below the main sequence at their stellar masses (~10^11 M☉). The reviewer's claim that these galaxies are 'above' the -1 dex line may reflect a misreading of the log-scale plot; the text's claim is consistent with the tabulated values showing these galaxies are quenched.

Section 4.1 states, "All members are located more than 1 dex below the star-forming main-sequence," while Figure 6 defines the comparison line as "the gray dashed line is the same sequence shifted by -1 dex downwards." However, the plotted overdensity members are not all below that dashed line, and Table 2 lists relatively high SFRs for some members (e.g., "DD-78 ... 6.9", "DD-76 ... 3.6", "DD-79 ... 3.2" M⊙ yr−1), so the universal claim is inconsistent with the figure/table.

The reviewer's claim is factually incorrect; Figure 6 and Table 2 confirm that all overdensity member galaxies (red stars and purple diamonds) are plotted below the dashed grey line (-1 dex below the main sequence). For example, DD-78 has a log SFR of ~0.84 at log M*=11.16, which sits below the -1 dex threshold at that mass (log SFR ~ 1.2), consistent with the text stating "All members are located more than 1 dex below the star-forming main-sequence".
